data.long_meaning: Derived from the Germanic elements ‘Rod’ (red) and ‘Gar’ (spear), Rutger’s name means ‘red spear’. It was a common name among the Frisians of the Netherlands and was brought to England by the Normans.

This spiritual significance is noted in the biblical reference of 'the rod of Aaron' that was used to part the Red Sea and protect the Israelites. seo.description_paragraph: The name Rutger, of Germanic origin, holds a significant place in both history and religion. Derived from the elements ‘Rod’ (red) and ‘Gar’ (spear), this name means ‘red spear’. Its popularity can be traced back to the Frisians of the Netherlands, a Germanic people who inhabited the coastal areas of the North Sea. The name Rutger was brought to England by the Normans, who heavily influenced the English language and culture.
